chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Mismaʿ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “It is disliked for a man—or the man is forbidden—to cast his urine from the rooftop into the open air.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man being addressed by the ruling
key_terms.بِبَوْلِهِ: with his urine; referring to urination
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is considered disliked in legal usage
key_terms.يُنْهَى: it is prohibited or forbidden by way of prohibition

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about urinating from a rooftop into the air?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal and ethical discouragement, or prohibition, regarding urinating from a rooftop into the open air. It reflects Islamic concern for cleanliness, dignity, and proper etiquette in matters related to taharah (ritual purity).
